overview: Songhai's wealth linked Gao and the Niger region to trans-Saharan commerce. Its surviving monuments make construction, religious practice and shared maintenance visible alongside the better-known history of its rulers.

items.text: At Gao, the Tomb of Askia combines an earthen pyramidal tower with mosque buildings, a cemetery and an assembly space.
Projecting wooden supports form permanent scaffolding. Renewing rain-eroded plaster is part of the building's continuing life.
During the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, Timbuktu was a center of Islamic learning and manuscript exchange.
Timbuktu's market brought together manuscripts, salt, gold, cattle and grain. Scholarship existed within a busy commercial city.
The mosques of Djingareyber, Sankore and Sidi Yahia preserve an earthen architectural tradition shaped by successive restorations.
